description:
Comments and Rustdoc in the workspace's Rust sources cite external papers, books, reports and standards by prose title. Each cited work has a key in the citation registry, so source documentation cites `@/citation/<key>` and `@/inv/external-claims-cited` holds.

## Background

The registry is `.jit/references.toml`. The source-comment sweep shortens comments and keeps evidence pointers; a prose citation without a registry key fails review. Prose citations reported so far include Seroussi (HPL-98-135), Rabin (1980), Swan, OEIS A011260, Dumas and Pernet, Granlund and Möller, Devegili et al. (ePrint 2006/471), Beuchat et al. (ePrint 2010/354), Gentleman and Sande (1966), Hacker's Delight, Goto and van de Geijn (2008), BLIS (2015) and 3GPP TS 38.212 and TS 38.214 editions.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Every external work cited by prose title, author or report number in a comment or Rustdoc block of a Rust file under `crates/` or `dev/tools/` has an entry in `.jit/references.toml` with complete bibliographic data verified against the publisher, the archive or the standards body.
- [hard] REQ-02: A linked record maps each cited work to its key and lists the files that cite it, produced by a committed command, and each key resolves as an item address.
- [hard] REQ-03: Editions and versions are distinct entries: a citation of one edition of a standard never resolves to another edition's key.
- [hard] REQ-04: No Rust source changes.
title: Register citation keys for external works cited in Rust sources
